Htr1e, a receptor that participates in the binding of these molecules, is thus indirectly connected to Oxymetazoline through the shared role of Htr1b. The scores from the paths indicate a moderate level of confidence in this relationship, supported by the sequential participation of Htr1b in the binding processes. The evidence suggests that Oxymetazoline may influence Htr1e through a pathway involving Htr1b, but further experimental validation is needed to confirm the direct interaction and functional significance. The mechanism appears to be biologically plausible, as it involves well-characterized receptors and binding events, though the exact role of Htr1e in this context remains to be elucidated.
